summary: Del Norte County, CA summit lookout house, called a Forest Service lookout house in 1941; a 1977 USGS note says it was destroyed and only the floor remained. FFLA lists it gone.

facts.design: Ground-level lookout house on the summit (FFLA list: Ground)
facts.status_note: 1977 USGS recovery note says the lookout house was destroyed and only the floor remained; FFLA list marks it Gone with no date
facts.agency: Six Rivers National Forest (Forest Lookouts lists Siskiyou National Forest first, then Six Rivers)

access.note: Reached on the Forest Service South Kelsey Trail #4E06; no closure stated in the sources read. No lookout structure to visit.

visit.trail_note: Hike the South Kelsey Trail #4E06: about 8 miles along the South Fork of the Smith River, then about 5 miles of steep climbing to Baldy Peak. The route beyond Harrington Creek has not been maintained for several years.

corrections.why: The Forest Service trail page for the route to Baldy Peak sits under Six Rivers National Forest, and the Peakbagging table lists the forest as Six Rivers. Forest Lookouts lists Siskiyou first, then Six Rivers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts lists the peak under Siskiyou National Forest, followed by Six Rivers. The Forest Service trail page and Peakbagging both use Six Rivers, so the proposed record uses Six Rivers.

The Peakbagging table tags removed lookouts with LO site, but its Baldy Peak row carries no such tag. The 1977 USGS recovery note describes the lookout as destroyed, and the 2020 trip report finds a square of rocks and scattered wood, metal and glass where it stood, so the record keeps gone.

notes_for_editor: Gone status is well supported (1977 USGS note, FFLA list, 2020 trip report). No source gives a build year, so no built event was added; the 1941 survey description is the earliest dated reference to the house. Elevation is not in the facts schema: Peakbagging lists 5775 ft (about 1760 m) as spot elevation, so the record's elevation_m could take 1760. The FFLA list gives no NHLR or FFLOS registration for Baldy Peak. Do not confuse with Baldy Mountain (Happy Camp) or Deadwood Baldy. The valhikes post is a personal trip report, so it is used only for the present-day burn and the square of rocks and scattered debris at the site. The trail page gives no current closure.
